blocks.text: Abbotsford Homes for Sale: streets and boundaries

items.t: Abbotsford is a single city in the Fraser Valley Regional District, crossed east–west by Highway 1 and Fraser Highway, with the Huntingdon / Sumas border crossing at its south end on the Highway 11 corridor.

The City publishes its communities as demographic profile areas, including Bradner – Mt. Lehman (area 1), Aberdeen (area 6) and West Abbotsford (area 7); board sub-area names and City profile names overlap but are not the same list.
Abbotsford International Airport (YXX) sits in the southwest of the city, south of Fraser Highway and west of Clearbrook.
Mission lies across the Fraser River to the north, the Township of Langley to the west, Chilliwack to the east, and the United States border to the south.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Homes for Sale: the housing stock

items.t: The city-wide stock is governed by Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw, 2014, No. 2400-2014, whose zone families run from the Section 200 agricultural zones (A1, A2) through urban residential zones such as RS3 and the infill RS7 zone to apartment and mixed-use zones.

Infill subdivision is an active form: Council reports in 2025 repeatedly rezoned single lots from Urban Residential Zone, Infill (RS3-i) to Infill Residential Zone (RS7) for two-, three- and four-lot subdivisions, for example at 2272 Lynden Street and 2330 Fir Street.
The rural half of the city is farm lots at agricultural scale: minimum subdivision lot area 8.0 hectares in the A1 zone and 16.0 hectares in the A2 zone.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Homes for Sale: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) is built into the OCP update: the draft framework received by Council on May 13, 2025 proposed an SSMUH 1 designation enabling small-scale multi-unit housing near the urban core and the Primary Transit Corridor, limited to three storeys and a maximum of four dwelling units per lot.

In the A1 agricultural zone, one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit per lot is permitted under the Agricultural Land Reserve Use Regulation, B.C. Reg. 30/2019, or with Agricultural Land Commission approval, on a lot of at least 0.4 hectares, capped at 90 square metres (lots of 40 hectares or less) or 186 square metres (larger lots), plus one secondary suite per lot to 100 square metres.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Homes for Sale: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Water and sewer are billed bi-monthly, not monthly, and a 5 percent discount applies if payment is received by the due date printed on the bill.
From January 2027, solid waste fees move off the annual property tax notice and onto the utility bill alongside water and sewer; collection days do not change.
Properties not connected to City water or sewer — well and septic properties — are not charged those utility fees.

Any utility account balance outstanding at December 31 is transferred to the property tax account and subject to daily interest, per the City's current utility bill page (stated for the 2025 balance).

Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Road, is the city's hospital, with 24-hour emergency, surgery and maternity services, and the urgent and primary care centre is at 100-2692 Clearbrook Road.
Property tax notices are billed annually for January to December, with an estimated delivery date of May 22, 2026 for the 2026 notice.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Homes for Sale: development and new projects

items.t: Abbotsforward 2050 OCP and zoning update, city-wide: the Stage 3 Draft Policy and Regulation Report was received by Council on May 13, 2025, with community engagement directed, and the City's laws site now carries the OCP as Bylaw No. 3690-2025. Status: adopted bylaw posted on the City laws site (as of November 3, 2026) for any later amendments.

McKee Neighbourhood Plan, for the Auguston and Highlands side of the city: the plan area currently holds about 4,600 people in 1,193 dwelling units, and the plan guides the phased build-out of the OCP's New Neighbourhoods area. Status: neighbourhood plan in force as an OCP schedule (as of November 3, 2026).
Status: construction west of the city, planning east (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Abbotsford Homes for Sale: costs and taxes

items.t: The City's 2026 Tax Rates Summary sets the Class 1 Residential general municipal rate at 1.08284 dollars per $1,000 of taxable value; the full 2026 rate is set by Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026 and adds school, Fraser Valley Regional District, hospital and library levies.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Homes for Sale: getting around

items.t: BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley system, not TransLink, runs Abbotsford buses; route 21 Fraser Hwy links Aldergrove and Bourquin Exchange via Highstreet Exchange.
Highway 1 interchanges serving the city include Mt. Lehman Road and Clearbrook Road; the Huntingdon / Sumas border crossing is at the south end of the Highway 11 corridor.
Abbotsford International Airport (YXX) is inside the city, in the southwest, under its own federal Airport Zoning Regulations, SOR/83-253.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Homes for Sale: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the specific lot in the City's WebMap for its zone and any Zoning Bylaw Schedule E floodplain designation before offering; both are lot-specific.

Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status is parcel-specific across the rural half of the city; subdivision, non-farm use and added dwellings can need Agricultural Land Commission approval on top of City zoning.
Airport height surfaces are a separate layer from zoning and floodplain: land on City drawing M-500 can be height-capped even where zoning allows a taller building.
